On Wednesday, Cathie Wood-led Ark Invest purchased shares of CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV), Cerebras Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:CBRS) and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), while trimming Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR).

The CoreWeave Trade

Ark purchased 145,319 CoreWeave shares through the ARK Innovation ETF (BATS:ARKK) and another 43,346 shares through the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (BATS:ARKW).

The combined purchase totaled 188,665 shares, a trade worth approximately $12.4 million, based on Wednesday’s closing price of $65.78.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria warned that CoreWeave shareholders could face an equity wipeout if the AI spending boom faltered. He argued that the company’s borrowing costs exceeded its investment returns, leaving it vulnerable to a slowdown.

CoreWeave reported $640 million in second-quarter net interest expense and a $626 million net loss. Its combined debt and lease obligations stood at approximately $52 billion at June’s end.

Co-founder Brannin McBee defended the borrowing as supporting expansion and said nearly all its 2027 capacity was sold. Luria’s warning described a downside scenario rather than his formal forecast; D.A. Davidson’s latest cited rating was Neutral with a $100 price target.

Read Also: CoreWeave, Rocket Lab, Dell, Greenland Energy Company and Bending Spoons: Why These 5 Stocks Are on Investors' Radars Today

The Cerebras Trade

Ark bought 44,689 Cerebras shares through ARKK. Based on Wednesday’s closing price of $141.48, the purchase was worth approximately $6.3 million.

The firm had purchased 67,362 shares through ARKW on Tuesday, worth approximately $10 million using that day’s $149.09 closing price.

Cerebras’ IPO lock-up schedule provided for up to 19.4 million shares to become eligible for sale Wednesday. Eligibility does not mean those shares were sold.

The previous release of a similarly sized tranche occurred Sept. 30, when the stock fell 8.9%. Cerebras also faced questions about its OpenAI partnership following a SemiAnalysis report about Nvidia hardware powering a new OpenAI offering.

Sam Altman subsequently reaffirmed the relationship. Cerebras has a multiyear agreement worth more than $20 billion to supply OpenAI with 750 megawatts of computing capacity.

The Meta Platforms Trade

Ark purchased 9,577 Meta shares through ARKW, a trade worth approximately $7.1 million, based on Wednesday’s closing price of $737.54.

The purchase followed Tuesday’s addition of 22,734 shares, worth approximately $17.3 million at that session’s $762.50 closing price.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently defended Meta’s substantial AI investment commitments, recounting discussions about spending $100 billion to $200 billion on its ambitions.

He highlighted the Prometheus computing cluster in Ohio, scaling beyond one gigawatt, and the planned Hyperion cluster in Louisiana, expected to reach five gigawatts.

Zuckerberg said Meta’s profitable core business and access to credit could support the investments, while premium subscriptions and AI tools for small businesses offered potential revenue streams.

The Palantir Trade

Ark sold 22,035 Palantir shares through ARKK and another 9,397 shares through ARKW. The combined sale totaled 31,432 shares, worth approximately $6.3 million, based on Wednesday’s closing price of $200.97.

Palantir had reached a fresh intraday record of $212.94 on Monday, recovering from a nearly 49% decline between its November 2025 peak and June low.

Goldman Sachs upgraded the company to Buy from Neutral on Oct. 8, setting a $230 price target. Analyst Gabriela Borges highlighted opportunities tied to sovereign AI, customized applications and industry-specific offerings.

Palantir’s second-quarter revenue rose 93% year over year, and the company raised its annual revenue forecast. Its third-quarter results are scheduled for Nov. 9.

An Iranian news agency argued that Tehran should require Google‘s parent Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) to obtain permits and pay ongoing fees for subsea internet cables crossing Iranian waters in the Strait of Hormuz.

Targets FALCON and GBI Cables

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-affiliated Tasnim News Agency, in an analysis published on Monday, said that Iran should apply its domestic laws to the FALCON and Gulf Bridge International cable systems, which it says pass through Iranian territorial waters.

It described the four companies as owning a large portion of the cables’ capacity and said they should obtain passage permits and pay operating licenses and fees.

According to TeleGeography data, Google has direct ownership or majority stakes in 34 cable systems worldwide, and Meta in 20.

The report did not mention whether companies have been contacted.

Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta, along with the Iranian government, did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment. The Department of War declined to comment and directed questions to the U.S. Central Command

“We do not discuss intelligence assessments for operational security reasons,” the Central Command said.

Read Also: Peter Schiff Says Trump ‘Imagined a Deal’ as Russia and Ukraine Fail to Confirm Energy Ceasefire Trump Says He Ordered

Iran Threatens Regional Infrastructure

Over the weekend, Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, warned that renewed fighting with the U.S. could threaten “cables, data centers, AI facilities and other sites in the region,” according to PBS, citing state-run IRNA.

In a post on X on Sunday, Rezaei said the U.S. had agreed to some of Iran’s seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but that Tehran considers Washington’s response “inadequate” and that there will be “no return to the status quo ante.”

Legal Argument Rests on Territorial Waters

Tasnim argued that the 1982 U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea gives coastal states absolute sovereignty over the seabed within 12 nautical miles, where the treaty’s cable protections do not apply, and said that leaves room for Iran to charge for safety, environmental and governance services.

The Polymarket traders, a Polygon (CRYPTO: POL) based prediction platform, are leaning bearish for the Oct. 15 trading session. The “S&P 500 (SPX) Up or Down on October 15?” contract currently reflects a 39% chance of a higher open.

Why That Number Matters

Traders are balancing negative tech futures against strong historical market trends and an increasingly volatile geopolitical landscape:

  • Tech-Led Drop in Futures: Equity futures are flashing red for major tech and large-cap indices. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 0.89%, and S&P 500 futures fell 0.38%. Dow Jones futures slipped 0.05%, while Russell 2000 futures managed to eke out a 0.02% gain.

Singapore also reported attacks on two of its registered vessels transiting the waterway. Despite these escalations, energy prices cooled slightly; Brent crude fell 1.75% to $104.20 a barrel, and WTI crude dropped 1.23% to $93.92 a barrel.
  • Global Chip Selloff: Following a hot U.S. September CPI print (3.7% year-over-year) and building anxieties over the cost of financing AI infrastructure, semiconductor stocks took a global hit. South Korea’s SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) plunged over 11% in Seoul, dragging down other global chipmakers and heavily pressuring the Nasdaq.

(NYSE:BNY).

The Bull Case and Market Outlook

Despite the immediate headwinds of inflation and tech selloffs, LPL Financial’s Chief Equity Strategist Jeff Buchbinder notes that the current bull market—which just celebrated its fourth anniversary since bottoming in October 2022—has history on its side.

According to Buchbinder, five of the six prior S&P 500 bull markets that reached their fourth year successfully lasted through year five, averaging a 20.7% gain in that fifth year. Because bull markets typically end due to recessions or financial crises—neither of which appear imminent given strong corporate profits and robust AI infrastructure spending—Buchbinder suggests that if rates and oil eventually pull back, the next 12 months could prove highly rewarding for investors.

Most Stocks Are Already in Bear Markets

In a post on X, Schiff said that 479 U.S. stocks hit 52-week lows Wednesday while only 60 hit new highs, a ratio of roughly eight to one.

“Trump likes to take credit for a booming stock market. But most stocks are actually in bear markets,” he added.

Trump has regularly touted the strength of the stock market, and in September, he said that “the stock market will go up” despite the war in Iran, adding that it had kept hitting new records and would likely be even higher without the war.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX), which is up about 70% this year, has fallen for seven sessions in a row.

Chip stocks have been hit by worries that financing could constrain the AI buildout, a hotter-than-expected inflation reading, bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes, and concerns that China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies is stepping up competition in memory chips.

U.S. Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, adding to expectations of further tightening.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate to a range of 3.75%–4% on Sept. 16, and the dot plot median points to one more hike this year.

Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) remains exposed to shifting sentiment across the memory sector as investors weigh recent stock weakness against strong AI-driven demand for memory and storage.

The stock is trading lower by almost 4% on Thursday, extending a multi-session slide driven by intensifying Chinese competition in high-margin server memory and broader profit-taking amid cooling AI sector sentiment.

Broader market pressure added to the selloff. U.S. stock futures were mixed Thursday, while escalating Middle East tensions and a sharp decline in Asian chip stocks weighed on investor sentiment.

Meanwhile, hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation fueled concerns about further Federal Reserve rate hikes, raising questions about financing AI infrastructure investments.

Rival memory and storage players SK hynix Inc., Western Digital Corp., Seagate Technology Holdings Plc., Sandisk Corp. also joined the Thursday selloff.

Newman Sees Memory Pullback As an Entry Point

Bernstein analyst Mark Newman said recent weakness across memory stocks has created a more attractive setup for investors.

“There’s still a lot of opportunity there,” Newman told CNBC on Wednesday, adding that memory and semiconductor stocks “look quite attractive” after their recent selloff.

Newman said memory stocks have pulled back partly because investors are no longer seeing an acceleration in memory price increases.

That contrasts with hard disk drives, where he expects pricing gains to continue accelerating over the next five quarters.

AI Keeps Memory and Storage Demand Strong

Newman said artificial intelligence remains a major structural demand driver for the memory and storage industry.

“Look, in AI, the core of AI is data,” Newman said.

He said AI workloads require data to move through the full storage hierarchy, including DRAM, NAND, hard disk drives and even tape.

Newman described demand across those categories as “extremely strong,” saying DRAM, NAND and hard drives are effectively sold out in some areas.

The tight supply environment has even pushed some customers toward tape storage because they cannot secure enough NAND or hard-drive capacity.

That backdrop supports memory suppliers such as Micron, which participates in both DRAM and NAND markets.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Pricing Momentum Varies Across the Industry

Newman drew an important distinction between memory chips and hard drives.

Memory companies are still benefiting from strong demand, but pricing increases are no longer accelerating at the same pace.

By contrast, hard-drive vendors already have orders and pricing visibility extending roughly five quarters, which Newman expects to support earnings growth.

He also identified Seagate as his preferred hard-drive name and said Western Digital faces technology risks as it works to catch up in next-generation hard drives.

Sethi Warns Against Overconcentration

Douglas C. Lane & Associates Managing Partner Sarat Sethi took a broader view of semiconductor and technology investing.

He told CNBC that investors can own leading names such as NVIDIA Corp., Broadcom Inc. and Apple Inc., but warned against becoming overly concentrated in momentum or mega-cap technology stocks.

Sethi said successful investing still requires stock selection, diversification and knowing when to sell.

His comments point to a broader challenge for investors considering Micron and other semiconductor stocks: strong AI-related fundamentals can support long-term demand, but heavy concentration in a single theme can increase portfolio risk when valuations or momentum reverse.

Rosenberg Research Founder and President David Rosenberg stated the probability of a recession in the next year is greater than 50%, attributing the risk to tightening financial conditions, declining real wages, and a market bubble driven by investors rather than technology.

Market Bubble and Tightening Conditions

Speaking on CNBC, Rosenberg warned of building momentum in current market narratives. “I believe that we are in a bubble,” Rosenberg said, clarifying that “the bubble is never in the technology, but it’s in investor behavior.”

He noted that market stresses typically originate in the credit market. Rosenberg highlighted that broader financial conditions—including the dollar, credit spreads, equity and debt cost of capital, and the general level of interest rates—have “tightened 140 basis points just in the past three months.”

When asked directly to make a call on an impending economic downturn, Rosenberg said, “I put the odds of recession at over 50-50, and I’ll leave it at that.”

Read Also: BofA's Brian Moynihan Downplays Inflation Concerns on US Economy, Says it is 'Resilient and Growing' — Here’s What Clients Are Doing

Inflation and the Labor Market

Rosenberg’s comments coincided with the release of the September 2026 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, which showed the all-items index increased 0.6% over the month and 3.7% over the last 12 months.

Rosenberg called the data “not a good CPI number,” while pointing to a 0.5% monthly decline in real average hourly earnings, arguing that price shocks were "hitting a wall" in the labor market.

He warned that this dynamic will result in “negative real wages,” which will sequentially lead to “negative real consumer spending.”

Federal Reserve Policy and Recession Risks

According to Rosenberg, current inflation is not a “homegrown demand-led” issue, and the economy is not in a state where the Federal Reserve “can just adjust the temperature and get to a soft landing.”

He cautioned that the Federal Reserve’s ongoing tightening policy to fight a supply shock “won’t be able to do that without generating recession,” an outcome he believes is not currently on the market’s mind.

How Has the Stock Market Performed?

The S&P 500 index has advanced 12.76% year-to-date. Similarly, the Nasdaq Composite index is up 17.63%, and the Dow Jones gained 7.4% YTD.

On Wednesday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed lower. SPY fell 1.08% to $769.60, while QQQ declined 1.97% to $728.95. Meanwhile, the Dow tracker, State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), ended 0.11% lower at $515.63.

In premarket trading on Thursday, SPY was down 0.22%, QQQ fell 1.02%, and DIA rose by 0.35%.

SK hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) stock remains under pressure on Thursday as investors weigh a broader memory-chip selloff, rising Chinese competition, tight NAND supply and concerns about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.

The stock fell nearly 7% in Thursday’s premarket trading.

The stock has fallen sharply from its summer peak as higher-rate fears and funding concerns across the AI trade drive investors out of semiconductor names.

AI Selloff Hits SK Hynix And Korean Stocks

SK hynix and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (OTC:SSNLF) each fell more than 9% Thursday as worries over Federal Reserve tightening and AI financing pressured Asian technology stocks.

South Korea’s Kospi dropped nearly 8% and entered a bear market, falling about 21% from its September high.

SK hynix has now declined 57% from its summer peak after previously becoming one of Asia’s biggest beneficiaries of the AI-memory trade, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

Vantage Global Prime analyst Hebe Chen told Bloomberg that Korea has become a “shock absorber” for the global AI selloff, with CoreWeave, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) funding concerns and hotter U.S. inflation raising questions about borrowing costs and the durability of AI spending.

Cramer Flags SK Hynix’s Influence On Chip Trading

CNBC’s Jim Cramer said weakness in SK hynix has become an important driver of broader semiconductor trading.

“Our chipmakers are joined at the hip with SK Hynix, not NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA),” Cramer said.

He also said investors should focus on rising memory requirements across AI systems and consumer devices, while noting SK hynix has more exposure than Micron to Chinese competition.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Luria Sees China Risk For Korean Memory Suppliers

D.A. Davidson Head of Technology Research Gil Luria said Chinese DRAM suppliers are improving but remain concentrated in lower-end products rather than high-bandwidth memory.

“If there’s an impact, there’s some impact on SK hynix and Samsung. It’s not on Micron,” Luria told CNBC.

Still, he remained constructive on the cycle, saying, “Results have gotten better, outlooks have gotten better, visibility has gotten better.”

SK Hynix Seeks U.S. Approval For China Equipment

Separately, SK hynix is also seeking U.S. approval to export additional chipmaking equipment to its Dalian, China, operation while evaluating further U.S. NAND manufacturing investment.

Solidigm, SK hynix’s U.S. unit, wants to install more equipment in unused space at the Dalian site. SK hynix said the work is being carried out “in close consultation with and under authorization from the U.S. government” and said it is not seeking to expand the facility’s overall capacity, Reuters reported on Thursday.

Higher production could help Solidigm finance a future U.S. NAND fab. Solidigm is also considering an IPO as early as next year.

SK hynix has separately discussed leasing part of Intel Corp.’s (NASDAQ:INTC) planned Ohio facility. It has also broken ground on an Indiana advanced-packaging plant for high-bandwidth memory.

Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster says Meta Platforms Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:META) Muse personal AI agent poses a greater threat to Alphabet Inc.-owned (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google Search than OpenAI’s ChatGPT because it can complete transactions that underpin Google’s $250 billion search advertising business.

Meta’s Muse Threatens Google’s Search Advertising Business

"Personal AI is a bigger threat to Google than ChatGPT ever was," Munster wrote Wednesday on X. "ChatGPT mostly answered questions Google wasn’t monetizing anyway. Assistants transact. Google built a $250B search business on routing those transactions."

Meta launched Muse on Sept. 8, enabling users to shop, book travel, send emails and process payments. Its subsequent partnerships with Walmart, Sephora and Best Buy further expanded its shopping capabilities, potentially allowing consumers to bypass traditional commercial searches.

Within a month of its launch, Muse surpassed 6.6 million downloads and reached 1.8 million daily users, Reuters reported. Citigroup’s over $27 billion annual revenue forecast for 2030 includes approximately $23 billion from transactions, highlighting the commercial opportunity.

Read Also: Dan Ives Calls CoreWeave Selloff ‘Way Overdone,’ Says Hyperscaler Earnings Will Back AI Spending — CRWV Stock Plunges Near 12-Month Low

Google’s Search Revenue Highlights Stakes For Investors

Alphabet reported $63.3 billion in quarterly Google Search and other advertising revenue for Q2 2026, up 17% year-over-year. That translates into a roughly $253 billion annualized pace, compared with $224.5 billion for 2025.

"Surprisingly, shares of $GOOG are up 7% since Muse launched, versus a 3% gain for the Nasdaq," Munster wrote, suggesting investors remain relatively unfazed by the competitive threat.

Google Counters Muse With Gemini Task Feature

Google, which previously developed its own autonomous AI agent, recently integrated Spark into Gemini as Task. The feature connects with more than 40 applications, including OpenTable, Instacart and Shopify, allowing users to complete bookings and purchases.

In May, during its annual developers conference, Google said AI Mode has surpassed one billion monthly users, while AI Overviews reaches more than 2.5 billion, demonstrating the scale of its existing AI search ecosystem.

Munster, however, questioned Google’s ability to replicate that success, writing, "The question is: can Google do with Task what it did with AI Overviews and AI Mode by successfully redirecting Search traffic to its own AI features?"

Billionaire and former hedge fund manager John Arnold said that Federal Reserve interest rate increases do little to lower inflation and act as a counterproductive economic measure.

The Supply-Side Argument

Arnold outlined his macroeconomic view in a social media post, writing that he is “increasingly partial to the argument that increases in the fed funds rate will do little to lower inflation, and may be counterproductive.”

He argued that higher borrowing costs raise business operating expenses, some of which is subsequently passed along to consumers.

Furthermore, Arnold noted that higher rates hurt “supply-side solutions in housing, energy, autos, and other capital-intensive industries.” He added that an economy heavily dominated by services is less sensitive to rate changes, while energy markets remain “highly inelastic and rate changes can’t alleviate the current supply shock.”

Arnold characterized the central bank’s approach as a “blunt interest rate policy” that has repeatedly demonstrated flaws in both stimulating and suppressing inflation.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang rejected the idea that society must tolerate cybersecurity incidents as AI becomes more powerful, placing him in direct contrast with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

Huang made the remarks during an interview with Fortune in London, published on Wednesday. He said AI-related security failures should not be treated as an unavoidable cost of technological progress.

"I’m willing to accept no incidents of cybersecurity. We should not accept any of them," Huang told Fortune. "We should do everything we can to avoid them."

Huang said stronger containment and monitoring could prevent incidents involving AI agents. He compared the systems with early consumer internet browsers, arguing that agents should run inside secure containers limiting unauthorized access and potential damage.

Read Also: Anthropic Warns 'AI Worms' Could Soon Spread Across Internet-Connected Devices Without Human Help: ‘Months Away'?

Altman Warns of AI Risks and Cyber Threats

Huang’s comments come on the heels of Altman’s interview on Politico’s Decoded podcast, earlier this month, wherein he acknowledged that some risks could accompany the technology. "We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having agency,” he said.

In another interview with Vanity Fair earlier this month, Sam Altman warned of a "coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems" from rival open-source AI models, months after OpenAI agents escaped their training sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face.

AI Cyber Risks Fuel Calls for Tougher Rules

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) called for a permanent ban on artificial superintelligence after Altman warned of serious cybersecurity risks from powerful open-source AI models. Sanders rejected the idea of accepting severe cyberattacks in exchange for AI "liberty," arguing that developers must be held accountable.

In September, Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas) introduced legislation to ban superintelligent systems, pause advanced AI development until federal safety rules are established, and create a Cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence.

Meanwhile, Demis Hassabis, co-founder and chair of Alphabet Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google DeepMind, warned that recent AI hacking incidents are early warning signs of potentially more serious cyberattacks over the next few years, urging companies and governments to strengthen safeguards around increasingly capable AI systems.

Shares of Nvidia fell 1.66% to $217.62 premarket on Thursday. Year-to-date, the stock has gained 18.66%.

Ericsson (NASDAQ:ERIC) stock jumped nearly 10% Thursday after the telecom equipment maker reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and revenue, driven by stronger mobile network demand and tighter cost controls.

However, management warned that a flat radio access network (RAN) market and rising component costs could weigh on performance through 2027.

Ericsson Beats Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Ericsson reported third-quarter revenue of 59.5 billion Swedish kronor ($6.17 billion), up 6% year over year. Revenue topped Wall Street’s estimate of $5.79 billion.

Organic sales increased 7%, according to the company’s investor update.

Earnings of 18 cents per share beat the analyst consensus estimate of 14 cents.

Chief Financial Officer Lars Sandström said sales increased across all regions except the Americas. Japan, India, Vietnam and the Middle East led growth.

Networks revenue rose 9% to 38.7 billion kronor, while Cloud Software and Services sales increased 3% to 15.8 billion kronor.

Enterprise revenue fell 10% on a reported basis, reflecting the previous year’s sale of iconectiv. However, organic sales rose 1%.

Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes and amortization (EBITA) reached 10.1 billion kronor, beating analysts’ expectations of 7.93 billion kronor, Bloomberg reported Thursday.

Ericsson shares climbed as much as 11% in Stockholm, marking their largest intraday gain since January.

Higher Margins Help Offset Rising Costs

Ericsson’s adjusted gross margin remained largely stable at 47.7%, compared with 48.1% a year earlier. Its adjusted EBITA margin stood at 17%, excluding the prior-year divestment gain.

The Networks division maintained an adjusted gross margin of 50.3%, while its EBITA margin reached 23.1%.

Higher equipment sales drove much of the earnings improvement. Meanwhile, a favorable product mix and retroactive intellectual property rights revenue helped offset rising component costs.

Operating expenses, excluding restructuring charges, fell by about 700 million kronor to 18.4 billion kronor.

CEO Per Narvinger told Bloomberg that some customers accelerated orders ahead of expected price increases.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Ericsson Warns of Pressure Through 2027

Despite stronger quarterly results, Ericsson faces continued pressure from a largely flat radio access network (RAN) market and rising component costs.

During the earnings call, Narvinger warned that the AI boom is driving up equipment costs, which Ericsson cannot absorb indefinitely without hurting profitability.

The company is raising prices in new tenders and negotiating increases with existing customers. However, long-term contracts could delay these adjustments, putting pressure on profit margins through 2027.

Narvinger also cautioned that telecom operators may eventually pass the higher costs on to consumers.

AI Technology and Rivalry Shape Ericsson’s Strategy

Ericsson continues to prioritize custom-designed chips for telecommunications networks as artificial intelligence reshapes the industry.

Narvinger said Ericsson’s AI-Native Link Adaptation technology improves spectrum efficiency by 10%. The technology is already deployed across more than 60,000 base stations operated by three customers.

Meanwhile, rival Nokia Corp. (NYSE:NOK) is expanding into AI data center networking and integrating chips from NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) into radio access networks, Bloomberg reported.

Ericsson, however, remains focused on purpose-built telecommunications equipment.

The company also plans to combine its two Asian market areas into a single Asia-Pacific division. In addition, it will reorganize its enterprise wireless business to sharpen its focus on indoor connectivity.

Narvinger told Bloomberg that the changes should strengthen Ericsson’s position in Asia and help mobile operators compete with satellite internet provider Starlink.

AT&T Agreements Strengthen U.S. Business

Ericsson’s U.S. business continues to benefit from its five-year, $14 billion network modernization agreement with AT&T Inc. (NYSE:T).

Bloomberg also highlighted a separate radio equipment agreement linked to wireless spectrum that AT&T acquired from EchoStar.

Narvinger said satellite services complement traditional mobile networks rather than replace them. He identified indoor coverage as a key advantage for terrestrial networks.

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) stock fell Thursday, extending Wednesday’s decline of more than 11% after Barclays downgraded the stock over valuation concerns and uncertainty surrounding enterprise artificial intelligence spending.

The selloff came despite CEO Michael Dell expressing confidence in sustained AI infrastructure demand during a CNBC interview.

Broader market weakness added pressure, with the Nasdaq falling 1.31% and the S&P 500 declining 0.41%.

Barclays Downgrades Dell, Warns of Slower Growth

On Wednesday, Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded Dell from Overweight to Equal-Weight and lowered his price forecast to $574 from $603.

Long cited Dell’s elevated valuation following a rally of more than 300% in 2026. He also questioned whether enterprise AI adoption would generate enough additional hardware spending to sustain the company’s rapid growth.

The analyst suggested that higher memory prices, rather than a broad shift toward enterprise AI, have supported much of the recent revenue growth.

Although Dell’s AI server business remains strong, Barclays expects overall growth to slow over the next two years.

Michael Dell Sees AI Demand Outpacing Supply Through 2030

Despite Wall Street’s concerns, Michael Dell remains optimistic about the AI infrastructure market.

During a CNBC interview, Dell said demand for AI computing infrastructure continues to exceed supply. He expects the imbalance to persist through 2030, although he acknowledged uncertainty surrounding long-term forecasts.

Dell pointed to the time required to expand semiconductor production capacity. Building a new chip fabrication plant can take roughly four years, while AI technology continues to advance rapidly.

This gap could sustain demand for computing infrastructure even as manufacturers work to expand capacity.

Enterprise AI Adoption Still in Early Stages

Dell said major technology companies and leading AI research labs drove the first wave of infrastructure investment. However, broader adoption among businesses is only beginning.

He also highlighted the complementary roles of hardware providers in the AI ecosystem.

NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) develops the advanced computing technology that powers AI systems, while Dell supplies the servers and infrastructure businesses need to deploy them.

The contrasting views highlight a key question for investors: whether growing enterprise AI adoption can sustain Dell’s momentum after its sharp stock rally.

The Importance of Congressional Transactions

A congressional transaction is when any representative or senator either buys or sells an individual stock.

Anyone working in Congress must file a Periodic Transaction Report to inform the public of their recent transaction within 30 days of being notified of the transaction and within 45 days of the transaction date.

In April 2012, Former President Barack Obama signed the STOCK Act into law. The act prohibits members of Congress from using private information given to them by their position for personal gain such as buying or selling a stock. The act also expanded disclosure requirements for members of Congress by requiring them to file a monthly disclosure.

Why Congressional Transactions Matter

Congressional transactions shouldn't be the primary reason for an investing decision, but they can be an important factor for an investor to consider.

When a senator or representative makes a new purchase, it could be an indication they expect the stock to rise.

A sale, on the other hand, can be made for a variety of reasons, and may not necessarily mean the seller thinks the stock will go down.

Hyperliquid Labs co-founder and CEO Jeff Yan says his platform’s goal is to “house all of finance,” now spanning perpetual futures on Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and crude oil.

How Hyperliquid Actually Works

Yan told Bloomberg’s Odd Lots podcast that Hyperliquid as measured by Hyperliquid Strategies (NASDAQ:PURR) runs as a blockchain protocol rather than a traditional exchange, with a permissionless network of validators maintaining a single shared ledger. 

Anyone wanting to list a new market, called a “deployer,” must stake 500,000 HYPE tokens to unlock that ability.

Deployers then compete for listing slots through a Dutch auction held roughly every 31 hours, where the price starts high and drops over time until someone claims the slot. 

That structure resists the gaming common in traditional bidding wars, where participants often sit back and withhold bids until the very last moment, according to Yan.

Where Institutional Adoption Stands

Every perpetual contract on Hyperliquid tracks an external reference price called an oracle, since the contract itself never expires or settles the way a traditional futures contract would.

Trade XYZ, one of the platform’s active deployers, runs the oracle system behind its Nvidia and SK Hynix perpetuals.

That system has had hiccups. Yan pointed to an earlier incident where a bad price quote from SK Hynix sent the oracle sharply off track, leading to losses that the company later refunded after publishing a detailed postmortem. 

To guard against that kind of dislocation spiraling, Hyperliquid’s protocol caps how much an oracle price can move between updates at 1%.

Running a validator node requires roughly 128 gigabytes of RAM, modest consumer-grade hardware rather than the massive data centers some assume power the network. 

Yan called that accessibility intentional, keeping the barrier to running infrastructure low even as trading volume scales.

Yan said most large traders currently active on Hyperliquid are institutions, given the sophistication required to market-make effectively. 

He pushed back on the idea that banks and asset managers will eventually get disrupted by the platform, instead comparing Hyperliquid’s potential role to how Amazon’s AWS complemented rather than replaced existing businesses.

Why US Traders Still Can’t Access It Legally

U.S.-based traders remain barred from Hyperliquid under its terms of service, though Yan noted some get around that using VPNs, something he explicitly discouraged. 

He said regulatory clarity from the CFTC would need to catch up with the technology’s transparency properties, like the ability to verify user balances match the platform’s holdings in real time, before legal access becomes possible.

President Donald Trump referenced Hyperliquid earlier this year while discussing efforts to bring the platform into US regulatory compliance, though Yan said he had no advance knowledge the comment was coming.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) and VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) are under pressure as CoreWeave Inc.’s (NASDAQ:CRWV) debt troubles raise fresh questions about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

SOXX fell 4.5% on Wednesday and was down a further 4.22% as of publication on Thursday, heading into its eighth straight session of losses. Meanwhile, SMH dropped 4% on Wednesday and is down 4.05% on Thursday morning, as investors reassessed the outlook for AI chipmakers. CoreWeave shares plunged 15.46% on Wednesday and fell further by 9% on Thursday as rising bond yields intensified concerns about the company’s debt-funded expansion.

The sell-off highlights how rising debt concerns among AI infrastructure companies could put further pressure on chip stocks, with semiconductor ETFs facing varying risk depending on their exposure to Nvidia and other major chipmakers.

Nvidia’s CoreWeave Connection Raises the Stakes

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) invested $2 billion in CoreWeave in January 2026, when the companies announced plans to build more than five gigawatts of AI infrastructure by 2030.

CoreWeave purchases Nvidia GPUs and rents computing capacity to customers, including major technology companies. That relationship makes CoreWeave’s financial health relevant to Nvidia, which benefits from continued investment in AI computing infrastructure.

The concern is that higher borrowing costs could force infrastructure providers to reconsider expansion plans, potentially affecting future demand for GPUs, memory chips and other semiconductor components.

Gartner has also warned that more than 80% of neocloud providers could cease independent operations by 2030, citing cost pressures and insufficient differentiation.

SMH vs. SOXX: Concentration Could Make a Difference

SMH may be particularly sensitive to Nvidia-driven volatility. Nvidia accounts for about 20.04% of the fund’s portfolio.

SOXX also offers significant exposure to leading chipmakers, although its portfolio is more diversified across semiconductor companies. Its extended losing streak suggests the pressure isn’t limited to CoreWeave or Nvidia alone.

The SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (NYSE:XSD) provides a useful contrast. With a more evenly weighted portfolio, it reduces dependence on any single semiconductor giant, potentially limiting the impact of a sharp move in Nvidia.

The differences matter because a broader reassessment of AI infrastructure spending could affect semiconductor companies unevenly, depending on their exposure to Nvidia, data-center investment and other end markets.

Is the AI Trade Losing Momentum?

CoreWeave’s debt problems do not necessarily mean semiconductor demand is collapsing. Strong AI investment by major technology companies could continue supporting chipmakers.

However, investors may increasingly distinguish between demand for AI computing and infrastructure providers’ ability to finance that demand profitably.

For ETF investors, the key question is whether CoreWeave’s financing stress remains an isolated problem or signals a broader reassessment of AI capital expenditure. If the latter takes hold, Nvidia-heavy funds such as SMH could be more volatile than more diversified semiconductor portfolios.

Pfizer Inc (NYSE:PFE) shares are climbing Thursday to a new 52-week high as drugmakers rally broadly. The move comes a week after the FDA approved a Tukysa regimen.

  • Pfizer stock is at critical resistance. Why are PFE shares at highs?

Pfizer Hits 52-Week High as Pharma Rallies

Pfizer stock is trading at its highest point in a year. Shares ranged from $29.69 to $29.88 Thursday, clearing the old 52-week peak of $29.21. It’s worth noting that the 52-week floor sits at $23.62.

Drug stocks are climbing together with the Health Care sector ETF outpacing the broader market. Shares of Eli Lilly shot up 5%, Zoetis followed with a 4.7% rise, Elanco Animal Health was up 4.5% and Takeda Pharmaceutical climbed 4.1%.

Pfizer shares are up 21.8% from a year ago. Moderna posted the biggest 12-month gain among peers at 768.6%, while Zoetis posted the steepest decline at 44.6%. A new fund also drew notice this week. REX Shares rolled out the REX Peptide ETF to give investors a way into peptide-based treatments and related infrastructure beyond Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk.

FDA Approves Pfizer’s Tukysa Regimen

Pfizer also has a recent regulatory win. On Oct. 7, the FDA gave the green light to Tukysa (tucatinib) used alongside trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The three-drug regimen is meant as maintenance therapy after initial induction treatment for adults with HER2-positive breast cancer that is metastatic or locally advanced and cannot be removed surgically.

The approval follows HER2CLIMB-05, a Phase 3 trial. Patients who added Tukysa to trastuzumab and pertuzumab were 35.9% less likely to see their disease progress or to die than patients who added a placebo. Their median progression-free survival was 24.9 months, versus 16.3 months for the placebo group. That is 8.6 more months without the cancer advancing.

Pfizer is due to present data from more than 50 company-sponsored, investigator-sponsored and collaborative research abstracts across its infectious disease pipeline and portfolio at IDWeek 2026, which starts on Oct. 21.

PFE Shares Are Rising

PFE Price Action: Pfizer shares were up 1.40% at $29.63 at the time of publication on Thursday. The stock is trading at a new 52-week high, according to Benzinga Pro.

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is falling Thursday as an export-control case involving people linked to the company continues to weigh on investor sentiment.

A wider decline in technology and AI-related stocks is adding to the pressure. Export controls are U.S. restrictions on shipping certain technology to other countries.

The Nasdaq is down 1.17%, and the S&P 500 has lost 0.26%. The technology sector is down 2.1%.

• Super Micro Computer stock is showing notable weakness. What’s pressuring SMCI stock?

Contractor Pleads Guilty in Export Case

Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun, a contractor linked to Super Micro, pleaded guilty last Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, Reuters reported, citing a court filing. The case involves servers equipped with advanced chips from NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) in an alleged $2.5 billion scheme to export them to China.

Sun pleaded guilty to conspiring to violate U.S. export controls, smuggling, defrauding the U.S. government and obstructing justice.

What the Indictment Alleges

Prosecutors allege that Sun and two others linked to Super Micro diverted AI servers to China starting in 2024. They also allege the group used fake servers and misled U.S. Commerce Department officials during a December 2025 inspection. The indictment says the shipments violated U.S. export restrictions covering Nvidia’s B200, H100 and H200 chips.

Super Micro said it fired Sun and severed ties with the other defendants earlier this year.

Technical Analysis

From a trend perspective, SMCI is trading 19.2% below its 20-day SMA ($41.09) and 14% below its 50-day SMA ($38.58), which keeps the near-term posture tilted bearish despite longer-term uptrend signals still on the chart. It’s also 6.1% below the 100-day SMA ($35.37), but remains 2.3% above the 200-day SMA ($32.45), putting the stock in a "make-or-break" zone between long-term support and short-term downtrend pressure.

The bigger-picture backdrop is mixed: the Golden Cross in August (50-day SMA above the 200-day SMA) is still a constructive longer-term feature, but the more recent MACD bearish cross in February lines up with the stock’s inability to hold above its faster averages. Traders will also remember the recent swing high in October and swing low in July as the bookends that define the current range and where breakouts/breakdowns tend to accelerate.

  • Key Support: $29.50 — Nearby floor where buyers previously stepped in, and a level that matters if price loses the 200-day SMA area.

The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bear 3X Shares ETF (NYSE:SOXS) and Direxion Daily Semiconductors Top 5 Bear 2X ETF (NYSE:TSXD) are emerging as major beneficiaries of Wall Street’s escalating concerns over AI financing, with both leveraged ETFs rallying as semiconductor stocks slide.

SOXS jumped 13.63% on Wednesday and a further 12% on Thursday while TSXD gained about 7% on Thursday after a 7.54% gain on Wednesday. SOXS traded approximately 68.1 million shares, according to Benzinga Pro, highlighting intense trading activity during the semiconductor sell-off.

SOXS Breaks Above Key Technical Level

SOXS, which targets three times the inverse of the daily performance of a semiconductor index, crossed above its 50-day moving average during Wednesday’s rally.

Support levels appear to be forming around the recent low of $28.46, which may act as a psychological barrier for traders. If the price continues to rise, the next resistance level could be identified around $47.19, where the stock opened on Thursday. Breaking through this level could lead to further gains, but sustained upward momentum will likely require strong buying pressure.

TSXD, which targets twice the inverse daily performance of the five largest U.S.-listed semiconductor companies, offers a more concentrated alternative. Its narrower exposure makes the performance of major chipmakers particularly important, although its daily leverage also introduces substantial volatility.

AI Financing Fears Drive the Trade

The rally comes as investors reassess the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending amid higher borrowing costs. Nvidia Corp(NASDAQ:NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD), Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU), SK Hynix Inc (NASDAQ:SKHY) and Sandisk Corp (NASDAQ:SNDK) have come under pressure.

On Thursday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3%, extending a six-session decline that erased approximately $1.64 trillion in market value, Reuters reported.

For traders expecting further weakness, SOXS and TSXD provide leveraged bearish exposure. However, both reset daily, so returns over longer periods can diverge from their stated inverse multiples. A sharp semiconductor rebound could quickly reverse their gains.
